The must-sees

  • Alter Markt

    Square

    Every 11 November at 11:11 the carnival season opens with crowds in costume on this square. The fountain honours Jan von Werth, a cavalry general of the Thirty Years’ War.

    Look for: High on a house front, find the Kallendresser, a small bronze figure baring his bottom toward City Hall.

  • Chocolate Museum

    Museum · 1993

    It opened in 1993, founded by the chocolate maker Hans Imhoff. Visitors can watch chocolate being made and taste from a chocolate fountain.

    Look for: Inside, a small tropical glasshouse grows real cacao trees.

  • Cologne Cathedral

    Church · 1880

    Building began in 1248, stopped for centuries with a crane left on the unfinished tower, and was completed in 1880. Behind the altar the golden Shrine of the Three Kings holds the relics that drew medieval pilgrims.

    Look for: In the south transept, Gerhard Richter’s window is made of thousands of small squares of coloured glass, partly arranged by chance.

  • Great St. Martin

    Church

    The church dates from the 12th and 13th centuries. Badly damaged in the war, it was the last of the city’s great Romanesque churches to be restored, in 1985.

    Look for: Inside, the east end has three rounded apses meeting in a clover-leaf plan.

  • Historic City Hall

    Civic building

    Cologne’s council has met on this spot since the Middle Ages. The tower was built in the early 1400s, and the arcaded loggia was added in the 1570s.

    Look for: Below the tower clock, find the Platzjabbeck, a carved head that opens its mouth and sticks out its tongue as the hour strikes.

  • Hohenzollern Bridge

    Bridge · 1911

    It opened in 1911 and was blown up by German troops in March 1945. Rebuilt after the war, it is one of the busiest railway bridges in Germany.

    Look for: At the ends of the bridge stand bronze equestrian statues of Prussian kings and German emperors.

  • KölnTriangle

    Viewpoint · 2006

    Completed in 2006, its viewing deck looks straight across the Rhine at the cathedral and the Hohenzollern Bridge. It is the classic view of Cologne’s skyline.

    Look for: From the deck, find the square tower of Great St. Martin to the left of the cathedral, rising above the old town’s riverfront.

  • Museum Ludwig

    Museum · 1986

    Opened in 1986, it grew from the collection of Peter and Irene Ludwig. It is known for its Pop Art and one of the largest Picasso collections in Europe.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Cologne and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Cologne passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
